builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops
summary: WATERFALL replaces manual reward engineering and privileged-information reward shaping with automated discovery: persona-conditioned generation of programmatic reward candidates, evolutionary Swiss-system tournaments judged by vision-language models over raw visual rollouts, and iterative mutation and pruning of candidates. The cost is a full population-based RL pipeline—many parallel rollouts, repeated VLM inference for judging, and longitudinal tracking of candidate histories—far beyond a single-GPU setup and dependent on paid VLM API throughput. It can fail if VLM judgments are noisy or biased (selecting degenerate reward hacks), if the tournament converges prematurely on brittle rewards, or if discovered reward programs overfit the evaluation environments and do not transfer.
rationale: The workflow requires population-based RL training over visual rollouts plus repeated VLM-judged tournaments, a compute and orchestration footprint that exceeds a single 24 GB GPU budget and is relevant only if the team actively trains RL agents in partially observable environments.
technique: Automated reward discovery via VLM-judged evolutionary tournaments
